title: Whitney Museum presents exhibition exploring Roy Lichtenstein's final year
summary: The Whitney Museum of American Art’s current exhibition Roy Lichtenstein: 1997 examines the final year of the artist’s life and work. Already an established painter and Pop artist, Roy Lichtenstein (1923–1997) continued to develop his studio practice at age 73, pursuing ambitious projects, including two mural commissions, several large-scale sculptures, and a new series of prints. The exhibition highlights a period of sustained innovation for Lichtenstein as he expanded his visual vocabulary while continuing to engage with many of the themes and image references that shaped his career. Bringing together studies, prints, models, and other ephemera, many from the Whitney’s collection, Roy Lichtenstein: 1997 offers a focused look at his experimentation and ongoing interest in new technologies and their effects on image making. title: Chrysler Museum of Art announces $2 million endowment for new Curator of Photography
summary: The Chrysler Museum of Art received a transformative $2 million gift from longtime Museum supporter and former curator Brooks Johnson to establish the Germaine Clair and Brooks Johnson curator of photography. The newly endowed position will ensure the continued growth, care and visibility of the Museum’s photography collection. The endowment honors Johnson’s late wife, Germaine Clair, an active member of Hampton Roads’ creative community known for her warmth, generosity, elegance and spirited advocacy for the arts. A highly accomplished graphic designer, Clair produced numerous books and exhibition catalogues for the Chrysler Museum of Art as well as W.W. Norton & Company, Bulfinch Press, Aperture and Takarajima Books. title: Joseph Bellows Gallery presents retrospective of photographer Declan Haun
summary: Joseph Bellows Gallery is presenting an exhibition of photographs by Declan Haun (1937–1994). A gifted photojournalist and perceptive observer of American life, Declan Haun worked at a time when the boundaries between documentary photography, journalism, and personal expression were becoming increasingly fluid. His photographs have the immediacy of eyewitness accounts, but they are also distinguished by a remarkable sense of composition, timing, and an understanding of human emotion. Haun began his professional career at the Charlotte Observer at the age of twenty-one. In 1963, he moved to Chicago, where he worked for the next fifteen years as a freelance photographer. title: Art intersects with material experimentation in Dark Side of the Moon exhibition at Sohn Fine Art
summary: Sohn Fine Art is presenting Dark Side of the Moon, a compelling group exhibition featuring photography and unconventional materials by Marieken Cochius, Chuck Kelton, Regina Durante Jestrow, and Jonathan Prince. The exhibition explores expansive territory where art intersects with material experimentation, revealing practices that move beyond the expected limits of each medium. The works offer a meditation on perception, transformation, and the enduring allure of the unknown. The exhibition is on view through October 5. Borrowing its title from the unseen hemisphere of Earth's celestial companion, Dark Side of the Moon invites viewers to consider what exists beyond immediate visibility. Rather than suggesting darkness as absence, the title points toward what remains unseen - hidden processes and the invisible forces that shape experiences. title: Barnes Foundation presents exhibition exploring Japanese American artists and postwar design
summary: In fall 2026, the Barnes Foundation will resent Noguchi to Asawa: Designing Postwar America, a groundbreaking exhibition that reconsiders 20th-century art and design within the context of Japanese and Japanese American incarceration during World War II and the broader history of Asian America. This exhibition will be the first to explore how this tumultuous era of Japanese American history formed a foundation for modern art and design in the United States. Conceived and curated by Cindy Kang, curator at the Barnes, this exhibition is on view in the Roberts Gallery from September 20, 2026, through January 10, 2027. Beauty and craftsmanship are hallmarks of midcentury Japanese American art and design. title: Emmanuel Louisnord Desir debuts new sculptures at Sebastian Gladstone Gallery
summary: Rough Ways of the Delicate Ones marks the second solo exhibition with Sebastian Gladstone Gallery by Los Angeles-based artist Emmanuel Louisnord Desir. Featuring eight new works, the exhibition continues Desir’s exploration of metamorphosis, endurance, and reclamation. Across these works, bodies and belief systems shift under pressures accumulated across time and generations. The exhibition takes its title from Baruch 4:26: “My delicate ones have gone rough ways, and were taken away as a flock caught by the enemies.” Desir considers delicacy not as weakness, but as a capacity for care, love, and righteousness—qualities made vulnerable by conditions that harden, corrupt, or lead one astray. His figures appear accordingly converted: amalgamations of bodies, creatures, machines, and symbols at once armored and exposed, guarded and reaching outward. title: Cédric Fauq appointed Curator of Contemporary International Art at Moderna Museet
summary: Cédric Fauq has been appointed Curator of Contemporary International Art at Moderna Museet and will assume his position on December 1, 2026. He is currently Chief Curator and Head of Programmes and Collections at Capc Musée d’art contemporain de Bordeaux. Previously, he held curatorial positions at Palais de Tokyo and Nottingham Contemporary. Tone Hansen, Director of Moderna Museet, says: "It is a pleasure to welcome Cédric Fauq to Moderna Museet. Cédric joins us at a pivotal moment as the museum prepares for its next chapter, where art, public art, architecture, and design come together. His experience, curiosity, and engagement with key artistic questions of our time will be a true asset as we build a new vision for the museum." Cédric Fauq was born in 1992 in France and holds an MA in Curating Contemporary Art from the Royal College of Art, London.His recent projects at the Capc Musée d’art contemporain de Bordeaux

title: David Zwirner presents major Roy DeCarava exhibition in Los Angeles
summary: David Zwirner opened an exhibition of photographs by Roy DeCarava curated by Ebony L. Haynes, at the gallery’s 606 N Western Avenue location in Los Angeles. On view is the sound i saw, DeCarava’s unwavering exploration of the relationship between the visual and the aural created between the late 1940s and the 1960s. Bringing together more than 130 images, this is the largest presentation of this body of work since its inaugural exhibition at the Studio Museum in Harlem, New York, in 1983. Presented in an adjacent gallery at 616 N Western Avenue is a listening room inspired by the artist’s work. Over the course of his more than six-decade career, New-York-born-and-based DeCarava produced a singular oeuvre of black-and-white photographs of modern life that combine formal acuity with an intimate and deeply human treatment of his subject matter. title: François Ghebaly presents Amol K Patil's Los Angeles debut exhibition
summary: François Ghebaly is presenting The Piled-Up Traces, Amol K Patil’s first exhibition with the gallery, and the first presentation of his work in Los Angeles. Following its debut at the 12th SITE SANTA FE International, curated by Cecilia Alemani, The Piled-Up Traces brings together Patil’s work in bronze, kinetic sculpture and drawing in an overarching, theatrical installation exploring class and caste-based exploitation. Patil’s work draws from the artist’s Dalit background and family’s history of activism: his grandfather was a poet, and his father an avant-garde playwright. Patil continues this tradition of protest, responding directly to the conditions of daily life in Mumbai’s chawls, dense housing complexes built in the 1900s to house migrant workers, which continue to be a locus of resistance within the Dalit community. title: Landmark exhibition unites U.S. Bicentennial photography surveys for the first time
summary: “Much Here Is Beautiful: Photography Surveys of the U.S. Bicentennial” at the Smithsonian American Art Museum brings together, for the first time, photography surveys that capture an expansive and evocative portrait of America in the years surrounding the 1976 U.S. Bicentennial. From the California coast to the Kansas heartland to the streets of New York City, the exhibition features images taken across the country by more than 70 photographers as part of the federally funded Surveys Grant Program. Bringing together 225 photographs, “Much Here Is Beautiful” places the Bicentennial images within the broader legacy of federal survey photography dating back to the 19th century and its lasting impact on generations of artists. “Much Here Is Beautiful” is the culmination of years of research, drawing on the museum’s rich photography holdings

title: Codex Azcatitlan returns to Mexico for first time in nearly 200 years
summary: Nearly two centuries after leaving Mexico, the Codex Azcatitlan has returned to the country for a temporary exhibition at the National Museum of Anthropology, where it is being shown as part of celebrations marking 200 years of diplomatic relations between Mexico and France. The exhibition, The Codex Azcatitlan. Mexico-France, 200 Years of Friendship, opened on September 17 and will remain on view through December 6, 2026. It marks the first time the manuscript has been exhibited in Mexico since it left the country in 1840. Produced in the Valley of Mexico in the late 16th and early 17th centuries, the Codex Azcatitlan is one of the most important surviving manuscripts documenting the history of the Mexica people. title: Ilse Van Roy and Frederic Geurts open joint exhibition Pas de deux at valerie_traan gallery
summary: Ilse Van Roy and Frederic Geurts have chosen the title Pas de deux for their joint exhibition at valerie_traan gallery. It is a term that actually originates from ballet. Two dancers, a man and a woman, move towards and away from each other in a duet. It immediately brings to mind Tchaikovsky’s The Nutcracker, perhaps the most famous pas de deux, first performed in 1892 in a choreography by Lev Ivanov. Now, I can well imagine that Ilse and Frederic would prefer, as a prototype, the pas de deux from Pina Bausch’s Vollmond (2006), because here classical ballet technique gives way to a bolder formal language – more anarchic, rawer, more direct. But if we look beyond the imposed virtuosity of classical ballet, we encounter here just as much the essence of the pas de deux: it is about the intense dynamic between man and woman, their complex quest that draws them irresistibly towards one another in an eternally paradoxical interplay of connection, separation and reconnection.

title: Fairfield University Art Museum opens exhibition exploring two centuries of Egyptomania
summary: Fairfield University Art Museum is presenting Hieroglyphs to Hype: The Modern Afterlife of Ancient Egypt, on view from September 18 – December 12, 2026, in the Museum’s Bellarmine Hall Galleries. This exhibition explores the enduring fascination with ancient Egyptian art and culture (dubbed “Egyptomania” by 19th-century Europeans) through a selection of paintings, prints, photographs, sculpture, and decorative art ranging from the early 19th century through the present day. These objects, from the humble to the refined, from the shamelessly commercial to the Afrofuturist, represent the range of artistic responses to—and misconceptions about—ancient Egyptian visual culture. Lenders to the exhibition include the Yale Center for British Art, the Wadsworth Atheneum, the Hood Museum of Art, and Yale University Art Gallery, in addition to artists and private collectors. title: Rome's Galleria d'Arte Moderna refreshes centenary exhibition with 25 additional works
summary: Rome’s Galleria d’Arte Moderna has refreshed its centenary exhibition, GAM 100. A Century of the Municipal Gallery 1925–2025, with 25 additional paintings and sculptures drawn largely from the museum’s holdings. The updated presentation, which opened on June 24, offers visitors a broader look at the evolution of the collection and at works that are rarely seen outside the museum’s storage areas. On view through October 11, 2026, the exhibition brings together more than 120 works tracing the history of the Galleria d’Arte Moderna and the development of Rome’s municipal collection. The museum’s holdings have been shaped by more than a century of acquisitions tied closely to the city’s cultural policies, beginning in the late 19th century and continuing to the present day. title: Paul Thiebaud Gallery celebrates 25th anniversary with San Francisco survey exhibition
summary: Paul Thiebaud Gallery announced the opening of 'Celebrating 25 Years at Paul Thiebaud Gallery', a survey of artists and works exhibited by the gallery over the past quarter century. Although not a comprehensive overview, the exhibition includes selected key artists and works from important exhibitions in the gallery’s history. The exhibition will be on view through November 7, 2026. Founded in 2001 by Paul LeBaron Thiebaud (1960-2010), the gallery began in a 1,000 square foot storefront space located at 718 Columbus Avenue in San Francisco, with administrative offices around the corner on Union Street. title: Randy Wray debuts hothouse-inspired abstractions in solo exhibition at Karma
summary: Describing the process of preparing for this exhibition over the last two years, Randy Wray referred to his studio as “a kind of hothouse where I’m growing paintings.” Sealed off from the world’s vicissitudes, the hothouse is a protective enclosure. Rare species flower and multiply in liquid-thick air. While retaining his characteristic earthy, virescent palette and organic forms, these new abstractions have a sharp, lustrous quality, as if crystallized in some sultry climate. Time is among Wray’s core materials. He works elliptically over long periods, leaving and returning to compositions, reconstituting select elements. His surfaces are dense and topographical, registering these intervals in tracts alternately burnished or matte, ridged or scarred. title: Scottsdale Museum of Contemporary Art presents two new desert-focused exhibitions
summary: Scottsdale Museum of Contemporary Art presents two new exhibitions that engage in a thought-provoking dialogue about differing relationships to the desert: one centered on expansion and displacement, the other on reciprocity and ecological knowledge. Model Home by alejandro t. acierto examines the impact of development and population growth, surveying how this expansion has altered the landscape and affected its human and nonhuman inhabitants, while asking who gets to keep home in the desert. What the Earth Keeps by Desert ArtLAB (April Bojorquez and Matt Garcia) imagines the land’s agency over human systems—consumption, domesticity, social hierarchy, colonial power—that attempt to control it, asking what happens if we listen to what the land already knows. title: Maastricht museum presents major tribute exhibition to photojournalist Eve Arnold
summary: Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof in Maastricht presents a tribute to the life and work of the legendary American photojournalist Eve Arnold (1912-2012) from 19 September 2026 until 31 January 2027. The large retrospective exhibition All about Eve features a selection of 130 iconic black-and-white and colour photographs from her impressive oeuvre, with a focus on the 1950s, 1960s, and 1970s. Eve Arnold is one of the most important photographers of the 20th century. In 1951, she became the first woman to join the prestigious Magnum Photos agency. Arnold was born in Philadelphia, lived in New York City, and moved to London in 1962. The photojournalist enjoys international acclaim for her social documentary and intimate celebrity photography. title: parrasch heijnen presents career survey of Los Angeles artist Charles Dickson
summary: parrasch heijnen is presenting Charles Dickson: Select Works, 1965 - 2026, the gallery’s first exhibition with the Los Angeles-based artist. Charles Dickson (b. 1947, Los Angeles, CA), whose sculptures and public installations explore the African American diaspora, is a significant member of the Black arts community of Los Angeles. Focusing on the artist’s deep experimental inquiry into material use, this exhibition includes work spanning Dickson’s more than sixty-year career. Integrating various processes and media, including wood, metal, bronze, Styrofoam, and acrylic, Dickson’s assemblage work utilizes disparate elements to engage in a dialogue about the politics of beauty. title: Raymond Meeks explores industrial relics and memory in new Casemore Gallery show
summary: Casemore Gallery is presenting Assemblage, an exhibition of recent photographs by Raymond Meeks. The exhibition presents pictures Meeks made of abandoned and ruined welding and wood-shop structures taken over 18 months at a worksite along the outskirts of Kingston, NY (in the hamlet of Cranesville, NY). In these images, we see his own active interventions among the detritus left behind, utilitarian relics from which he created provisional sculptures and aesthetic compositions, temporary assemblages for the camera that breathe a second life and new consideration into the formerly quotidian. title: Tony Rizzi presents most comprehensive exhibition of his photographic work to date
summary: "Now I begin my life in Frankfurt. I really like it here and feel like I should be here. I feel like there’s a protective presence by my side at all times…strange. WORK HARD, DON’T LIE, AND TRY NOT TO HURT ANYONE." - Excerpt from Tony Rizzi’s diary (September 7th, 1985) This quote frames the most comprehensive exhibition to date of the renowned US-American dancer, choreographer, and photographic artist Tony Rizzi (*1965, USA). For the first time, this exhibition offers deeper insight into Rizzi’s intuitive photographic practice to date. From his early black-and-white photographs and distinctive Polaroids and photo collages to his recent video works. His oeuvre on display demonstrates the versatility of his artistic practice. title: Benton Museum of Art opens Saul Steinberg Foundation gift exhibition
summary: The Benton Museum of Art at Pomona College announced its fall exhibition “Give Them a Riddle”: Gifts from The Saul Steinberg Foundation, on view from August 22, 2026, to January 3, 2027. While best known for his drawings in The New Yorker magazine, Steinberg is also renowned as a leading twentieth-century artist, philosopher, and cultural critic. Featuring more than 60 works across multiple media recently given to the museum by The Saul Steinberg Foundation, this exhibition traces Steinberg’s inventive artistic practice over five decades, during which he developed a distinctive, playful graphic language that he skillfully employed to satirize and critique the cultural habits and conditions of the post–World War II era. “With profound gratitude to The Saul Steinberg Foundation, we are thrilled to present a wide range of works by Steinberg,

title: Vanessa Amoah Opoku and June Drevet collaborate on Synthesizing Realities exhibition
summary: What connects us to a home, to others, and to where we come from, even across distance? How do images come into being that not only depict but also forge relationships? Synthesizing Realities takes its starting point from the eponymous artist’s book, which we—the artist and the critic—developed in 2025 and 2026, and in which we synthesized our perspectives on the relationship between our bodies and technologies, on digital sensing, and decolonial forms of photographic images. In our conversations, Vanessa Amoah Opoku’s installations took center stage. For several years now, the artist has been deliberately using sensing technologies that embody colonial logics. title: Hirshhorn debuts major sculpture by Elmgreen & Dragset
summary: The Smithsonian’s Hirshhorn Museum and Sculpture Garden has announced the acquisition of a monumental new sculpture by Elmgreen & Dragset, an artist duo celebrated for large-scale installations that investigate the complexity of societal norms and structures. Commissioned for the Sculpture Garden, “Eight” (2026) extends the artists’ decades-long preoccupation with the pool motif. Cast in stainless steel with a lacquered cyan interior, and furnished with a diving board, ladder and lights, “Eight” evokes ideas of leisure through the form of a typical backyard pool. Upended, empty and eternally unswimmable, the 28-foot-tall sculpture emblematizes the artists’ mastery of displacement—excerpting familiar objects from people’s surroundings and presenting them as new and strange.
